articleTitle: Directly modulated laser transmitter for access/metro applications
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We review our recent achievements in directly modulated laser (DML) transmitters for access/metro applications. Especially, we present the use of DC-balanced line coding to greatly improve the system performance of frequency modulated DML transmitters. Also presented in this paper is the use of duobinary coding to accommodate high-speed signals using low-bandwidth DMLs.

articleTitle: Efficient light confinement to λ/10 spot sizes in optical fibre tips
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: Light confinement beyond the diffraction limit has been achieved in optical fibre tips. We successfully fabricated a gold-coated optical fibre tip with wedge-shaped apex for the efficient excitation of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). An improved transmissivity higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> and spot sizes of the order of λ/10 have been obtained by optimizing the overall light throughput along the fibre tip.

articleTitle: Large-scale self-healing architectures for fiber Bragg grating sensor network
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: In this paper, two large-scale self-healing architectures for fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensor networks are proposed and demonstrated. We design branch nodes by using simple optical switches and couplers to reconfigure the FBG sensing subnets if any link fails. Moreover, to increase the number of sensors that could be multiplexed in the structure, we adopt a lxN switch or fiber delay lines of different length to concatenate all the sensing subnets. Finally, we analyse the capacity of the proposed architectures in theory.

articleTitle: Negative group velocity superluminal propagation in optical fibers using stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We demonstrated the superluminal propagation at negative group velocity using stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in optical fibers. In the scheme, the Stokes wave is circulated back into the ring cavity for Brillouin lasing to enhance the peak loss. The experiment demonstrated the superluminal light propagation can be realized by increasing the input signal power. The largest time advancement of 221.2ns has been observed. Correspondingly, the negative group velocity is -0.15c and the group index is -6.636.

articleTitle: Multiband UWB optical system technical research
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: HG is a principal interface device to connect digital home devices of private domain to access network of public domain. HG in the paper is with optical interface as a backbone network access and with UWB interface as an Ad Hoc services access. MB UWB signal based analogy sub-carriers modulation modulates Laser Diode with intensity modulation. OCML consists of an open ended microstrip line with a GaAs substrate as E/O demodulator. The device performance of GaAs substrate is better than that of Ge-on-Si, SiGe/Si, and Si. The research shows that the system with these components is much feasible.

articleTitle: Improvements of twin-core fiber optical tweezers' performance
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: The techniques of optical trapping and manipulation of neutral particles by lasers, provide unique means to control the dynamics of small particles. These new experimental methods have played a revolutionary role in areas of the physical and biological sciences. This paper reviews the implementation of optical tweezers. At first the basic structure of the twin-core fiber optical tweezers is introduced which has an abrupt tapered shape. Several simulations have been carried out to completely investigate its performance and review the effects of different factors. These parameters include applied phase shift between input electric fields, wavelength and waist of laser beam and grating profile of fiber's cores. All of the investigated parameters are some useful tools which can guide the designers for the best design.

articleTitle: Ultra-high on/off ratio optical switch based on SOI-SOA waveguide: Numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: A novel device is presented and simulated to perform the all optical switch by utilizing the cascaded silicon on insulator (SOI) and semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) optical waveguides, in which both controlling and signal pulses are co-propagating. Simulation results show that the all optical switch behavior with ultra-high on/off ratio can be easily achieved by adjusting the initial delay time (the negative initial delay-signal pulse before controlling pulse, and the positive initial delay-signal pulse after controlling pulse).

articleTitle: Live cell index sensing based on the reflection mode of tilted fiber tip with gold nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We presented a micrometer size tapered fiber tip for real-time refractive index measurement of live cell. The tip is cut with a specific tilted angle. Only the cutting surface of tip apex is coated with gold nanoparticles (GNPs) by selective bonding method. The evanescent wave at the apex will excite the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of GNPs. With enhanced scattering at the resonance wavelength, the tip reflection will experience a loss, which is analogous to attenuated total reflection (ATR). By measure the reflection beam, a wavelength dependent loss dip in the reflection spectrum or an intensity loss of a specific wavelength could be used to detect the refractive index of live cell.

articleTitle: Dynamic optical network system for adapting the diversification of services
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: This paper proposes the novel network design concept 'Dynamic optical network system' which is different from current networks design 'Static optical network system'. Proposal can adapt various applications, services with quite different characteristics such as bandwidth, latency, so can reduce the network power consumption drastically against the current networks and realize the high efficient use of network resource.

articleTitle: Routing and wavelength assignment in optical networks with fairness consideration
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: The routing and wavelength assignment (RWA) problem with fairness consideration is discussed in this paper. Based on an existing traffic classification and wavelength reservation scheme, an enhanced wavelength reservation scheme with fairness consideration is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate the better performance of the proposed scheme in terms of optimizing traffic connection fairness and reducing average traffic blocking probability.

articleTitle: Active photonic crystal fiber amplifiers and lasers
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: The advent of photonic crystal fibers with their novel optical properties has brought many significant advantages to the field of high power fiber lasers and amplifiers, which are gaining more and more interest for different applications. Er and Yb-doped large mode area are particularly promising, since they allow to reach high power levels avoiding nonlinear effects, and to greatly improve the thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: Advances in optical reflectometry for diagnoses of optical devices and networks
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: Following a review of recent advances in the development of optical reflectometry, a novel optical coherence domain reflectometry (OCDR) by use of an optical frequency comb (OFC) source is proposed and demonstrated with high spatial resolution (<; 10 cm), large dynamic range (>;45 dB), and short measurement time (≤ 10 s).

articleTitle: All-optical wavelength conversion and clock division utilizing semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We numerically and experimentally demonstrate a technique for performing all optical wavelength conversion with simultaneous clock division based on the period-one oscillation and cross-gain modulation effect in an optically injected semiconductor laser. Through the numerically simulation, the results that 18 GHz divided optical clock with wavelength down conversion of 5 nm can be obtained from 2 × 18 Gb/s optical time division multiplexed data stream. Moreover, the dependence of output signal on signal light strength, probe light strength, wavelength detuning, and bias current are also investigated, respectively. A proof-concept experiment is demonstrated with 12.4 GHz optical clock division and 4.33 nm wavelength down conversion. The experimental results are consistent well with that of the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A polarization-independent depolarizer with high isolation
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: A novel optical passive device combining the abilities of isolation and depolarization, named isolating depolarizer here, is presented. It would be used in polarization sensitive systems to restrain the polarization-dependent noise and also isolate the light in the reverse direction. For the DFB laser with linewidth of 0.1nm, experiment results show that the output degree of polarization, insertion loss and polarization dependent loss of the device are 3.2%, 1.35dB and 0.1dB, respectively. In the wavelength range of 1550±20nm, the minimum isolation of the device is 34.5dB. The device proposed here would be a compact and low-cost alternative when both depolarization and isolation are required simultaneously.

articleTitle: Wavelength control and spectral narrowing of high power fiber lasers using volume Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We report on the novel use of volume Bragg gratings for effective spectrum narrowing and wavelength control of high power Tm-doped fiber lasers in the 'eyesafe' 2 μm spectral region. Over 130 W of diffraction limited output has been yielded with a spectral linewidth of ~ 10 pm. The operating wavelength was continuously tunable from 1926 to 1998 nm, with >; 110 W output power over a tuning range of 68 nm from 1930 nm to 1998 nm. A relatively narrow linewidth of ~ 2.0 pm (FWHM) has been generated using a grating pair in serial configuration. Simultaneous dual-wavelength operation has been demonstrated by combining volume Bragg gratings of different specifications and using a simple resonator configuration for wavelength selection. The prospects for further improvement in performance will be discussed.

articleTitle: Fiber laser sensor with beat frequency demodulation
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: An improved multi-longitudinal mode fiber laser sensor formed by a fiber Bragg grating, a piece of Erbium-doped fiber and a fiber reflector is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. By using a fiber reflector, the presented sensor system has higher SNR and lower threshold than the original fiber sensor system with two FBGs. Experimental results show that strain sensitivities are -0.697 KHz/με @ 915 MHz and -1.31 KHz/με @ 1713MHz, respectively. The root mean square deviations are about 3.2 με@915 MHz and 2.5 με@1713 MHz.

articleTitle: A new optical code translation scheme for multi-hop network and simulation of multi-user asynchronous OCDMA system
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: Transparent optical code (OC) translator is an indispensable component to realize multi-hop and code-reuse in optical code division multiple access (OCDMA) as well as OC-label based optical packet switching (OPS) networks. In this paper, we propose a scheme for transparent OC translation based on superstructured fiber Bragg gratings (SSFBGs), and present the simulation result of 10 Gb/s 7-hop transmission by utilizing such OC translators. We also implement the simulation experiment of 8-user 5 Gb/s asynchronous OCDMA network and obtain decoded signals with distinct autocorrelation peak at matched receivers.

articleTitle: Polarization independent single photon detection approach based on quasi-phase-matched sum frequency generation
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: Polarization independent sum frequency generation (SFG) is proposed in an electro-optic (EO) tunable periodically poled Lithium Niobate (PPLN). The PPLN consists of four sections. External electric field could be selectively applied to them to induce polarization rotation between the ordinary and extraordinary waves. If the domain structure is well designed, the signal wave with an arbitrary polarization state could realize efficient frequency up-conversion as long as a z polarized pump wave is selected. The applications in single photon detection and optical communications are discussed.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated quad machzehnder IQ modulator for generation of advanced optical modulation formats
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We propose and fabricate a monolithically integrated quad Mach-Zehnder in-phase quadrature (QMZ-IQ) modulator, where four sub-Mach-Zehnder (sub-MZ) modulators are arranged in an IQ super-structure and integrated in a single LINbO3 substrate. By feeding different electronics and operating at different bias conditions, it has been deployed to synthesize several different advanced optical modulation formats, like 20- and 80-Gb/s minimum phase-shift keying (MSK), 40-Gb/s quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK), and 40-Gb/s quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM).

articleTitle: A voice recording system based on distributed fiber laser
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: A voice recording system based on distributed feedback fiber laser (DFB-FL) is presented in this paper. We record and recover voice signal by interrogating the DFB-FL wavelength shift, derived from the change in the external environment around the DFB-FL. Voice recording is demonstrated using both unifrequent voice signal and human voice respectively, and satisfying results have been obtained. The system provides high precision, stability, anti-interference and security to hazardous gas. Therefore, it has promising prospects in coal mine and hazardous gas surroundings.

articleTitle: Solar cells based on atomic layer deposition
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: The advantages of atomic layer deposition (ALD) include highly controlled deposition parameters, deposition uniformity, ultra-precise film thickness and good step coverage. Its prominent characteristics have drew attention to researchers in the fields of solar cells. The heterojunction, core-shell structure and surface passivation of solar cells can be preparated by ALD to get better system performance. For example, the photoelectric conversion efficiency is improved by reducing electrons and holes recombination and protecting the cells to fulfill the utilization of energy.

articleTitle: Optical inverse-RZ duobinary format for high-speed optical transmission
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: We investigate a new optical modulation format, namely inverse-return-to-zero duobinary, for optical transmission. Its various methods of signal generation as well as its dispersion tolerance in optical transmission are discussed and compared.

articleTitle: Preparation and spectral properties of the Yb3+ doped silicate glass
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: The Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> doped laser glass composed of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-Li<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-Na<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-MgO-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Yb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> were studied experimentally using the absorption and fluorescence spectrum. And the various spectral parameters of samples were calculated by the reciprocity method, including the absorption cross section, stimulated emission cross-section and fluorescence life time. The result shows that the alkali metal oxides possess different influence on the spectrum and laser parameters of the laser glass. Furthermore, Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> doped lithium silicate glass has the larger absorption and emission cross-section and the lower fluorescence lifetime. The kind of glass can inhibit concentration quenching and improve laser performance, which is a high performance laser material for the application of photonic crystal fibre laser.

articleTitle: A building structure health monitoring system based on the characteristic of TFBG
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: This paper introduces a new method of central wavelength of migration detection in fiber Bragg grating sensors based on the transmission properties of the main mode and side mode of Tilted fiber Bragg grating, and make it into a building structure health Monitoring System. In order to separate temperature effect with fiber Bragg grating, we use two adjacent FBG (one was used for sense, another for reference) which have the same central wavelength but different grating length, by parallel connection to make a sensing probe. Fix the TFBG keep on to a PZT, which was applied a zigzag sweep voltage in 10 Hz. Then the main mode and side mode of TFBG periodically offset in the same direction, so that the spectrum signal from sensing probe can be demodulated. The photodiode makes the transmitted light intensity changed into electric current. Voltage is amplified to 0~5v by amplifier circuit. Then set the voltage to A/D card for data acquiring and analytical processing data for real time display of await strain. Experimental results show that it is feasible to demodulate action spectrum by TFBG (the resolution of micro-strain detection is 5 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">με</sup> ), which solved the cross sensitivity of FBG to temperature and strain. The scheme may serve as the important technical guarantor that change the planned overhaul mode to premonitory one for building structure, and it will finally realize the intelligence of anti seismic and reducing disasters. The system is stably and reliable, low cost.

articleTitle: Optical microfiber passive components
publicationTitle: 9th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN 2010)
abstract: A review of passive components based on optical microfibers is presented.
